question: In which patient population is HbA1c UNRELIABLE for diagnosing or monitoring diabetes?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Age alone does not render HbA1c unreliable. It can be used in elderly patients in the absence of confounding conditions.

Correct. HbA1c reflects average glucose over the red cell lifespan (~120 days). In haemolytic anaemia (also iron-deficiency anaemia, thalassaemia, G6PD deficiency), shortened RBC lifespan falsely lowers HbA1c. Use FPG or OGTT instead.
ACE inhibitors do not affect haemoglobin glycation or RBC lifespan. HbA1c remains reliable in hypertensive patients.

While CKD can cause anaemia, it is haemolysis (not simply CKD stage 3) that specifically undermines HbA1c reliability. Use clinical judgement — severe CKD with haemolytic uraemic changes warrants caution.

overallFeedback.feedback: HbA1c is unreliable when red cell lifespan is shortened or abnormal haemoglobin variants are present: haemolytic anaemia, iron-deficiency anaemia, thalassaemia, G6PD deficiency, pregnancy (second/third trimester).
Well done — haemolytic conditions shorten RBC lifespan and produce a falsely low HbA1c. Always use FPG or OGTT in these patients.
